chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one in Ihram who shortens (hair/nails) from some parts and does not shorten from others, he said: It suffices him.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.يُجْزِئُهُ: It suffices him / It is valid for him
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: Shortens (referring to cutting hair or trimming nails)

ai.seo_question: Does a person in Ihram need to trim all hair or nails evenly, or is partial grooming sufficient?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies a specific fiqh detail regarding the permissibility of partial grooming (such as trimming hair or nails) while in the state of Ihram, ruling that the act is valid (yujzi'uhu) even if not performed uniformly across all areas. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in ritual obligations, distinguishing this partial act from the complete prohibition of removing hair or nails entirely during Ihram. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith through figures like Jamil ibn Darraj and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari.
